rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warns people against the withdrawing whisperer, which tests them to reveal who does the best deeds.
rows.anchor: عن الحكم بن عمير الثمالي رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says waswasa first begins during ablution.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي رضي الله عنه قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal says urinating in the washing place causes waswasa.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مرة
rows.claim: Ibn Murra says waswasa is most persistent with the person who sees it at work within himself.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مرة رضي الله عنه قال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's supplication asks God to fill his heart with remembrance and drive Satan's whisper away.
rows.anchor: عن معاوية بن أبي طلحة قال

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: Muawiya likens Satan to a weasel at the heart's opening: it whispers, withdraws when God is remembered, and returns when one is silent.
rows.anchor: عن معاوية في قوله : { الوسواس الخناس } قال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says Satan places his snout on a person's heart; remembrance makes him withdraw, while forgetfulness lets him seize the heart, hence the name الوسواس الخناس.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet describes the whisperer's birdlike beak entering the heedless person's heart-ear to whisper; remembrance makes it retreat, which explains the name الوسواس الخناس.
rows.anchor: عن أنس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan crouches on a person's heart, whispering during heedlessness and withdrawing when God is remembered.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { الوسواس الخناس } قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every newborn has waswasa upon the heart; remembrance makes it withdraw, heedlessness makes it whisper, and al-Hakim authenticated this report.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ما من مولود يولد إلا على قلبه الوسواس

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd defines al-khannas as one who alternates between whispering and withdrawing, and says this applies among jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال : الخناس الذي يوسوس مرة ويخنس مرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that the human devil is more harmful because people see him directly, whereas the jinn devil whispers unseen.
rows.anchor: وكان يقال : شيطان الإِنس أشد على الناس من شيطان الجن

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir says waswasa has a doorway in a person's chest from which it whispers.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى بن أبي كثير قال

rows.speaker: عروة بن رويم
rows.claim: Urwa reports that Jesus prayed to see Satan's place in a person and saw a snake-headed figure on the heart; it withdrew when God was remembered and whispered otherwise.
rows.anchor: عن عروة بن رويم أن عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام دعا ربه أن يريه موضع الشيطان من ابن آدم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima locates waswasa in a man's heart, eye, and sexual organ; in a woman it is in her eye, vulva when she approaches, and anus when she turns away.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : الوسواس محله على فؤاد الإنسان
